_comment: Design-time Screen Memory Load, produced offline by tools/complexity-agent. The engine looks these up; it never scores a screen at runtime. Unseen screens fall back to neutral (45) and are queued for offline scoring, so the cache self-warms.
_model: azure-openai, temperature 0, fixed rubric + 3 few-shot examples

com.thread.demo/Step1Details._note: The rubric has no term for layout, so the multi-column rows below are recorded but do not move the score. The scan cost is real and currently unmeasured.
offendingElements: Two fields on one row, then three on the next: no single column to scan
Three controls across truncates their labels
Currency sits beside Estimated cost but is a separate decision with no default
Employee ID has to be looked up and the screen does not say where
Cost centre picker: 25 options, unsorted, no default, no search
Budget code and GL account: two similar-looking codes from different systems
Percentage split appears only after 'Fixed percentage' is chosen
Project / WBS element is optional but nothing on screen says so
Validation reports one error at a time, so fixing one reveals the next
'Apportionment basis', 'GL account', 'WBS element' - jargon, undefined on screen
Submit is irreversible and does not say so

com.microsoft.office.excel/SheetView._note: Neutral fallback. Excel renders the grid on a custom surface, so the accessibility tree is sparse here. Interruption and return detection is unaffected - it needs only the package name - which is why the hero scenario works on Excel regardless.
